methods.label: Multiply by the decimal percentage
methods.levelReason: Converting a percentage and multiplying a decimal by an integer are within Grade 6 scope.

methods.label: Take one quarter
methods.explanation: Since \(25\%=\frac{25}{100}=\frac14\), finding \(25\%\) means taking one of four equal parts. Each part is \(80\div4=20\), so \(25\%\) of \(80\) is \(20\).
methods.levelReason: Recognizing a quarter and dividing by four use the same or lower prerequisite level than decimal multiplication.

candidate.annotationRationale: The route-neutral target is finding a specified percentage of a number, p196. Both methods use percentage conversion, recorded as shared support p195. Method 1 uses decimal-by-integer multiplication, p132. candidate.changeReason: 25% equals 0.25, and 80 times 0.25 is 20. The current calculation is sufficient; the separate quarter method offers an accessible equal-sharing interpretation.

review.mathematicalCheck: Method 1 correctly computes \(80\times0.25=20\). Method 2 independently uses \(25\%=1/4\) and \(80\div4=20\), with equal sharing correctly explained.
review.levelCheck: Both methods fit Grade 6; the quarter method uses elementary fraction meaning and division.
review.methodDistinctness: Taking one equal quarter supplies a useful interpretation distinct from decimal multiplication.
